issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award should not be set aside for inadequate notice where the affected party received notice, had a reasonable opportunity to participate, and failed to show that the procedure prevented the presentation of their case or caused serious prejudice.
material_facts: The arbitration involved numerous parties, extensive business and property disputes, and an agreement authorising the arbitrator to manage the proceedings and proceed ex parte after reasonable notice.
The objector had attended earlier arbitration meetings and taken an active part in the proceedings.

The arbitrator sent a circular directing the parties to attend a further meeting and provide information, followed by a telegram asking the objector to attend a later meeting and warning that proceedings would continue in his absence.
The objector did not say that the notified dates were unsuitable, that he had difficulty attending, or that he had requested an adjournment.
The proceedings relied on documentary evidence; no party presented oral evidence requiring cross-examination.
The objector did not claim that his interests were adverse to those of the co-sharers who attended.
issues.conclusion: The objector was not denied a fair opportunity to participate, and the award could not be set aside on the ground that he lacked reasonable notice.
issues.legal_principle: A party to arbitration must receive a reasonable opportunity to present their case, but has no unfettered right to dictate the hearing arrangements. The arbitrator may manage the hearing and proceed in a party’s absence after proper notice. Natural justice is flexible and depends on the circumstances; a complaint ordinarily requires proof of real prejudice, not merely a technical breach. The Court relied on the arbitration agreement’s provisions empowering the arbitrator to set procedure and proceed ex parte after reasonable notice, and on Montrose Cannel Foods Ltd. v. Eric Wells (Merchants) Ltd., British Oil and Cake Mills Ltd. v. Horace Battin & Co. Ltd., The Chairman, Board of Mining Examination v. Ramjee, Union of India v. Anand Kumar Pandey, R.S. Dass v. Union of India, M.C. Mehta v. Union of India, State of U.P. v. Harendra Arora, Managing Director, ECIL v. B. Karunakar, State Bank of Patiala v. S.K. Sharma, Aligarh Muslim University v. Mansoor Ali Khan, U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad v. Gyan Devi, and Renusagar Power Co. Ltd. v. General Electric Co. No statutory provision was identified as the basis for this ruling.

rule.if: arbitration_award_challenge and notice_of_hearing_given and opportunity_to_participate_available and not inability_to_attend_shown and not serious_prejudice_shown

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: The proceeding challenges an award made in arbitration.
predicates.notice_of_hearing_given: The arbitrator notified the party of the hearing or meeting at which the matter would proceed.
predicates.opportunity_to_participate_available: The party had a reasonable opportunity to attend and present their case.
predicates.inability_to_attend_shown: The party showed that circumstances outside their control prevented attendance or presentation of their case.
predicates.serious_prejudice_shown: The party showed that the alleged procedural failure caused serious prejudice to the presentation of their case.

issues.definition: When an arbitration award is challenged, notice and an available opportunity to participate, without proof of inability to attend or serious prejudice, mean that the notice is treated as reasonable and the award is not set aside on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A party’s personal relinquishment of a natural-justice objection does not establish that other parties were denied a fair opportunity; each complaining party must establish denial of justice to themselves.
material_facts: One objector filed an application unequivocally withdrawing his objections to the awards and asking that the awards be made rules of court.
That objector sought to resile from the withdrawal only after maintaining that position for several years.
The other parties who complained of procedural unfairness had participated in the arbitration proceedings.
The objector did not establish that the other parties’ interests were adverse to his or that his interests had not been safeguarded by those who attended.
issues.conclusion: The objector could not resile from his express withdrawal, and the other parties could not rely on his personal objection; each had to prove that the arbitrator denied them justice.
issues.legal_principle: A party may relinquish a natural-justice objection expressly or, in an appropriate case, by conduct. A defence personal to one party is not available to others merely because they were involved in the same proceeding; each party alleging denial of a fair opportunity must show that they were otherwise unable to present their case, rather than having failed to use an opportunity available to them. The Court relied on Minmetals Germany GmbH v. Ferco Steel Ltd. and Renusagar Power Co. Ltd. v. General Electric Co.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: The proceeding challenges an award made in arbitration.
predicates.one_party_expressly_withdrew_objection: A party expressly withdrew their objection to the award or arbitration procedure.
predicates.other_party_relies_on_that_objection: Another party invokes the withdrawn objection as the basis for their own challenge.

issues.definition: When one party expressly withdraws an objection and another party relies on it, the other party must prove that justice was denied to them personally.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator’s request that parties promise not to challenge an award does not invalidate the award where the request was not acted upon and no such promise was given.
material_facts: The arbitrator asked the parties to provide a letter stating that they would not challenge the award.
No party issued the requested letter, and the request was not acted upon.
issues.conclusion: The request did not render the award a nullity.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the unacted-upon request as insufficient to invalidate the award in the circumstances, noting that the arbitrator may have sought to bring the disputes to an end. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: The proceeding challenges an award made in arbitration.
predicates.arbitrator_requested_nonchallenge_promis: The arbitrator asked the parties to promise that they would not challenge the award.
predicates.no_promise_given: The parties did not give the requested promise.

issues.definition: When an award is challenged after the arbitrator requested a promise not to challenge it, the absence of any promise means that the request did not invalidate the award.

issues.legal_issue: An auction conducted in an unrelated recovery proceeding should not be stayed in an appeal concerning the validity of an arbitration award.
material_facts: An application sought to stay an auction of company properties being conducted at the instance of a bank under a recovery certificate issued by a debt recovery tribunal.
The auction concerned enforcement of a mortgage and guarantee in a dispute between a third party and a company.
The Court found that the recovery proceeding had nothing to do with whether the arbitration award should be set aside.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to intervene in the auction through the arbitration appeal, vacated its interim stay, and left the parties to pursue remedies available in law.
issues.legal_principle: An appeal concerning an arbitration award is not the forum to pursue relief in a separate recovery proceeding that is unrelated to the validity of the award. The Court cited no earlier case or statutory provision for this ruling.

predicates.arbitration_award_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the validity of an arbitration award.
predicates.auction_arises_from_separate_recovery_pr: The auction is being conducted in a separate proceeding to recover a debt or enforce security.
predicates.auction_unrelated_to_award_validity: The auction does not concern whether the arbitration award is valid.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning an arbitration award, an auction in a separate recovery proceeding that is unrelated to the award’s validity is not stayed through that appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A court hearing an appeal confined to a limited question about an arbitration award should not determine a separate request for appointment of a receiver when the matter may be pursued before an appropriate forum.
material_facts: The legal heirs of certain respondents applied for appointment of a receiver.
The appeals raised a limited question concerning the arbitration proceedings and award.
issues.conclusion: The Court made no order on the receiver application and stated that the parties could apply to an appropriate forum if the need arose.
issues.legal_principle: Relief beyond the limited question before the appellate court should be sought through an appropriate proceeding before the appropriate forum. No earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this ruling.

predicates.arbitration_award_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an arbitration award.
predicates.receiver_request_raises_matter_beyond_ap: The request for a receiver concerns a matter beyond the limited issue before the appellate court.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning an arbitration award, a receiver request beyond the appeal’s scope is left for an appropriate forum.

issues.legal_issue: A court need not adjudicate contempt allegations involving disputed facts in a long-pending appeal and may leave the parties to pursue an appropriate proceeding in the executing court.
material_facts: A contempt petition alleged that parties had violated interim court orders by surrendering tenancy rights and through other acts.
The appeal had remained pending for a long time, and the allegations raised factual disputes.
No order had previously been made on the contempt petition; the matter had only been directed to be considered at the final hearing.
issues.conclusion: The Court made no order on the contempt applications and observed that an appropriate proceeding could be initiated before the executing court if the occasion arose.
issues.legal_principle: Where contempt allegations require resolution of disputed facts in a long-pending appeal, the appellate court may decline to determine them in that appeal and leave the parties to an appropriate proceeding. No earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this ruling.

predicates.arbitration_award_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an arbitration award.
predicates.contempt_allegations_raise_factual_dispu: The contempt allegations depend on factual matters disputed by the parties.
predicates.appeal_long_pending: The appeal has remained pending for a long time.

issues.definition: In a long-pending appeal concerning an arbitration award, disputed factual contempt allegations are left unadjudicated in that appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A party who has maintained for years an express position withdrawing objections may not change counsel at a late stage to resile from that position.
material_facts: A party applied to withdraw objections to the awards and maintained that position for several years.
The party later sought to change counsel while seeking to resile from the withdrawal.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not permit the party to change counsel at that stage and made no order on the relevant applications.
issues.legal_principle: In the circumstances, the Court declined to permit a late change of counsel where the party had maintained the position underlying the withdrawal for several years. No earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this ruling.

predicates.pending_award_appeal: The proceeding is a pending appeal concerning an arbitration award.
predicates.party_maintained_withdrawal_position_for: The party maintained an express position withdrawing objections over an extended period.
predicates.late_counsel_change_sought_to_resile: The party sought to change counsel at a late stage in order to resile from that position.

issues.definition: In a pending appeal, a late request to change counsel to resile from a withdrawal position maintained over an extended period is not permitted.
